passage: I'm Ayesha, at the next desk in the design team. For weeks Kavitha had looked worn out. Then on Thursday at the tea point I saw her and Rohit talking in low voices. Rohit was showing her notes on his phone; then she showed him hers. I caught "dates", "same words" and "same here", and by the end her shoulders had come down and she laughed once. When I asked later, Kavitha only said, "Facts, not gossip." She told Rohit not to do anything on her account, and he agreed they would only go to HR if both wanted to. I can't say exactly what she feels, and I don't know the whole story, but she looks lighter than she has in a month.

qa.q: Where did Ayesha see Kavitha and Rohit talking?
qa.a: Ayesha saw them at the tea point on Thursday.

qa.q: What might Kavitha have felt as she compared notes with Rohit?
qa.a: She may have felt relief that it was not just her, since her shoulders came down and she laughed once, though Ayesha admits she cannot say exactly.

qa.q: How can two colleagues support each other in a situation like this?
qa.a: They can share facts and dates rather than gossip, and support each other without pulling anyone into a risky move, as Kavitha and Rohit agreed.

qa.q: How might Rohit have felt while sharing notes?
qa.a: Rohit may also have felt relief at finding he was not alone, since Ayesha heard "same here" and Rohit agreed to go to HR only if both wanted to.

grounding: A coworker admits facing the same treatment and Kavitha and Rohit quietly compare facts, feeling relief without a risky move.

passage:

Nirmala: wait. yes. every Thursday
Uday: I thought it was just me. I've been feeling like I'm bad at this job
Nirmala: same!! I've been keeping a list of the times, just for myself
Uday: honestly that's such a relief to hear 😌
Nirmala: let's be careful though. facts only, not gossip about him
Uday: agreed. I'll start writing mine too. date, time, what he asked
Nirmala: and let's not drag the new trainees into it unless they want. they're on probation
Uday: yes. no pressure on anyone
Nirmala: if it keeps happening, we could each go to HR with our own notes
Uday: that feels less scary with two of us
Nirmala: talk tomorrow at lunch 🙂

qa.a: Mr. Joshi makes Nirmala redo reports every Thursday.

qa.q: What was Nirmala feeling on learning that Uday faced the same thing?
qa.a: Nirmala felt relieved and less alone, realising the late-night redos were not just about one person.

qa.q: What is it like for Uday to hear Nirmala has the same problem?
qa.a: Uday feels relieved, having started to believe he was simply bad at the job.

grounding: A chat shows two coworkers discovering the same treatment, feeling relief, and agreeing to share facts, not gossip, without pulling others into risk.

passage: At the dairy cooperative's collection centre outside Anand, the supervisor, Mr. Parmar, had a habit of shouting at whoever handled the evening milk register. For weeks Devika thought it was about her slow handwriting. Then one evening, waiting for the last tanker, Sahil from the testing counter said quietly, 'He yelled at me for forty minutes last month. I stopped sleeping properly.' Devika felt her shoulders loosen for the first time in weeks. It wasn't just her. They sat on the steps and compared dates, not rumours: she had four, he had three. 'Don't ask the others to join in,' Sahil said. 'Ramila-ben has a small baby, she can't risk anything.' Devika nodded. 'Just facts. And we each keep our own notes.' They agreed that if it went on, each of them would speak to the society's secretary with what they had written. Then the tanker's lights came up the road.

qa.q: How many dates did Devika have?
What was Devika feeling when Sahil admitted the same treatment?
qa.a: Devika felt relieved, her shoulders loosening, knowing it wasn't just her.

qa.q: What made their way of comparing notes wise?
qa.a: They shared dates rather than rumours, kept Ramila-ben out of any risk, and planned to each speak to the society's secretary.

qa.q: What has the shouting been like for Sahil?
qa.a: Sahil has been badly shaken, even losing sleep after being yelled at for forty minutes.

grounding: Shows a coworker admitting he faces the same shouting, the relief of not being alone, and comparing facts without drawing others into a risky move.
